description: Agilent Technologies, Inc., incorporated in Delaware in May 1999, is a global leader in life sciences, diagnostics and applied markets, providing application-focused solutions that include instruments, software, services and consumables for the entire laboratory workflow. Following a November 2024 reorganization it reports three business segments: Life Sciences and Diagnostics Markets, whose activities span specialty contract development and manufacturing services for pharmaceutical customers and reagents, instruments, software and consumables that enable clinical and life sciences research; Agilent CrossLab, which spans the entire lab with services, consumables, software and laboratory automation; and Applied Markets, comprising gas chromatography, gas chromatography mass spectrometry, remarketed instruments, spectroscopy and vacuum divisions.

Apple Inc. designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells a variety of related services. Its products include iPhone smartphones based on the iOS operating system, Mac personal computers based on macOS, iPad multipurpose tablets based on iPadOS, Apple Watch, AirPods and Beats products, Apple Vision Pro, its spatial computer based on visionOS, and Home products including Apple TV 4K, HomePod and HomePod mini. Its services include advertising through third-party licensing arrangements and its own advertising platforms, a portfolio of fee-based AppleCare service and support products, and cloud services that store and keep customers' content up to date and available across multiple Apple devices and Windows personal computers.

AbbVie Inc. is a global, diversified research-based biopharmaceutical company, incorporated in Delaware in April 2012 and spun off from Abbott Laboratories in January 2013, whose product portfolio holds leadership positions across immunology, neuroscience, oncology and aesthetics. It operates as a single global business segment dedicated to the research and development, manufacturing, commercialization and sale of innovative medicines and therapies, supported by a global research and development and supply chain organization, with commercial marketing, sales and distribution organized by geographic region or therapeutic area.

Airbnb was founded in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has grown into a global community of over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2.5 billion guest arrivals in almost every country and region across the globe. It operates a global marketplace connecting guests with stays, experiences and services in over 220 countries and regions, with offerings expanded to include services and redesigned experiences launched in May 2025, and it focuses on five key stakeholders: its employees, shareholders, hosts, guests and the communities it serves. Key strategic priorities include making its service better, bringing Airbnb to more parts of the world and expanding what it offers.

Abbott Laboratories is an Illinois corporation incorporated in 1900 whose principal business is the discovery, development, manufacture and sale of a broad and diversified line of healthcare products. It operates through four reportable segments: Established Pharmaceutical Products, Diagnostic Products, Nutritional Products, and Medical Devices. Established Pharmaceutical Products comprise branded generic pharmaceuticals manufactured worldwide and marketed outside the United States in emerging markets, with portfolios in gastroenterology (Creon, Duphalac, Duspatal), women's health (Duphaston, Femoston), cardiovascular and metabolic therapies (Lipanthyl, TriCor, Synthroid), and pain and central nervous system medicines. In November 2025 Abbott entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Exact Sciences Corporation, which is expected to enable it to enter the cancer diagnostics market.

Arch Capital Group Ltd. is a publicly listed Bermuda exempted company and a member of the S&P 500 index that provides insurance, reinsurance and mortgage insurance on a worldwide basis through its wholly owned subsidiaries. While positioned to provide a full range of property, casualty and mortgage insurance and reinsurance lines, it focuses on writing specialty lines of insurance and reinsurance, and had approximately $26.9 billion in capital at December 31, 2025, writing $16.5 billion of net premiums and reporting net income available to Arch common shareholders of $4.4 billion in 2025, with book value per share of $65.11 at December 31, 2025 compared to $53.11 per share a year earlier.

Accenture plc is a leading solutions and global professional services company that helps the world's leading enterprises reinvent by building their digital core and unleashing the power of AI, bringing together the talent of its approximately 779,000 people, its proprietary assets and platforms, and deep ecosystem relationships. It manages its business through three geographic markets, the Americas, EMEA and Asia Pacific, and goes to market by industry across five industry groups covering communications, media and technology, financial services, health and public service, and products and resources, delivering two types of work, Consulting and Managed Services. Its Reinvention Services bring together capabilities across strategy, consulting, technology, operations, Song and Industry X. Revenues are derived primarily from Forbes Global 2000 companies, governments and government agencies, with more than 9,000 clients and fiscal 2025 revenues of $69.7 billion.

Adobe Inc. builds software platforms and tools that empower everyone to create, providing solutions for creativity, productivity and personalized digital experiences that form the foundation of digital experiences and span the content workflow from the first creative spark through creation and production to personalized delivery across every channel. It serves business professionals, consumers, creators, creative professionals and marketing professionals with an end-to-end integrated platform spanning ideation, creation, production and activation, powered by Adobe's AI platform, and is weaving generative and agentic AI capabilities across its offerings through its commercially safe Firefly foundation models, an extensive ecosystem of partner models, and customer-customized models trained on licensed and public domain data.

Analog Devices, Inc. is a global semiconductor leader dedicated to solving customers' most complex engineering challenges, delivering innovations that connect technology to human breakthroughs and play a critical role at the intersection of the physical and digital worlds by providing the building blocks to sense, measure, interpret, connect and power. It designs, manufactures, tests and markets a broad portfolio of solutions, including integrated circuits, software and subsystems that leverage high-performance analog, mixed-signal and digital signal processing technologies, spanning data converters, amplifiers, power management, radio frequency integrated circuits, edge processors and other sensors, and it sells its products globally through a direct sales force, third-party distributors, independent sales representatives and its website in approximately 50 countries.

Archer-Daniels-Midland Company and its subsidiaries unlock the power of nature to enrich the quality of life, and are an essential global agricultural supply chain manager and processor that provides food security by connecting local needs with global capabilities, as well as a premier human and animal nutrition provider and a leader in health and well-being products. It partners with thousands of farmers around the world to purchase their crops and uses its integrated global origination, logistics and manufacturing network to transform many of those raw commodities into an expansive array of products serving the food, feed, fuel, and industrial and consumer products sectors, offering a broad portfolio of food and beverage products from staple foods to natural colors and flavors, plant-based proteins and lower-sugar, fat and salt solutions, plus nutrition ingredients and health and well-being products such as probiotics, enzymes and supplements.

Automatic Data Processing, Inc. was founded in 1949 to help clients focus on their business by solving their payroll challenges, and in the 77 years since has led the Human Capital Management industry in innovation, being the first in HCM to deliver automation, move to the cloud, provide a mobile app and create an online marketplace, and today building artificial intelligence into the core of how it orchestrates, governs and executes HR and pay processes. It describes itself as a trusted, service-driven and AI-enabled partner for HCM and a global leader in HR and payroll solutions, serving over 1.1 million clients and paying over 42 million workers in over 140 countries.

Autodesk, Inc. is a global leader in 3D design, engineering and entertainment technology solutions, spanning architecture, engineering, construction, product design, manufacturing, media and entertainment. Its customers design, fabricate, manufacture and build anything by visualizing, simulating and analyzing real-world performance early in the design process, which allows them to foster innovation, optimize their designs, streamline manufacturing and construction processes, save time and money, improve quality, deliver more sustainable outcomes, communicate plans and collaborate with others. Its professional software products are sold globally through a combination of indirect and direct channels, and its product families include Tandem, a cloud-based platform that transforms the built asset lifecycle and helps architecture, engineering, construction and operations firms harness BIM data to create and hand over a digital twin, and AutoCAD, a customizable and extensible CAD application for professional design, drafting, detailing and visualization.

Ameren, formed in 1997 and headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, is a public utility holding company whose primary assets are its equity interests in its subsidiaries, which are separate, independent legal entities with separate businesses, assets and liabilities, and dividends on Ameren's common stock and the payment of expenses by Ameren depend on distributions made to it by its subsidiaries. Its principal subsidiaries are Ameren Missouri, which operates a rate-regulated electric generation, transmission and distribution business and a rate-regulated natural gas distribution business in Missouri; Ameren Illinois, which operates rate-regulated electric transmission, electric distribution and natural gas distribution businesses in Illinois; and ATXI, which operates a FERC rate-regulated electric transmission business in the MISO.

American Electric Power Company was incorporated under the laws of the State of New York in 1906 and reorganized in 1925, and is a public utility holding company that directly owns all of the outstanding common stock of its public utility subsidiaries. The service areas of those subsidiaries cover portions of Arkansas, Indiana, Kentucky, Louisiana, Michigan, Ohio, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia and West Virginia, and they have traditionally provided electric service, consisting of generation, transmission and distribution, on an integrated basis to retail customers, with restructuring laws in Michigan, Ohio and the ERCOT area of Texas causing previously integrated regulated rates to be unbundled in those states.

Incorporated in 1981, AES is a global energy company accelerating the future of energy, delivering greener, smarter energy solutions and partnering with large corporate customers on their strategic energy transitions while meeting their current energy needs. It has over four decades of experience developing, operating and owning electric generation and utilities, and is a leading provider of renewable energy to data center companies, particularly in the U.S., and to large mining companies outside the U.S. It operates two lines of business, generation and utilities, through its Renewables, Utilities, Energy Infrastructure and New Energy Technologies strategic business units, and measures their performance using Adjusted EBITDA.

Aflac Incorporated was incorporated in 1973 under the laws of the state of Georgia, and together with its subsidiaries provides financial protection to millions of policyholders and customers in Japan and the United States. Its principal business is supplemental health and life insurance products, with the goal of providing customers the best value in supplemental insurance products in Japan and the U.S., paying cash benefits fairly and promptly for eligible claims when a policyholder or insured gets sick or hurt. The Company is authorized to conduct insurance business in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, several U.S. territories and Japan.

American International Group, Inc. is a leading global insurance organization that provides insurance solutions helping businesses and individuals in over 200 countries and jurisdictions protect their assets and manage risks, through AIG operations, licenses and authorizations as well as network partners. It executes world-class underwriting and claims expertise through franchises that are among the leaders in their geographies and segments, serves millions of clients ranging from individuals to small and medium-sized businesses to multi-national Fortune 500 companies, and has broad and long-standing distribution relationships with brokers, agents, advisors and marketplaces. It has a global workforce of more than 22,000 colleagues and approximately $41 billion in shareholders equity.

Assurant, Inc. was incorporated as a Delaware corporation in 2004 and is a premier global protection company that partners with the world's leading brands to safeguard and service connected devices, homes and automobiles, leveraging data-driven technology solutions to provide exceptional customer experiences. It operates in North America, Latin America, Europe and Asia Pacific through two operating segments: Global Lifestyle, which provides mobile device solutions, extended service contracts and related services for consumer electronics and appliances, credit and other insurance products referred to as Connected Living, and vehicle protection services, commercial equipment protection and other related services referred to as Global Automotive; and Global Housing, which provides lender-placed homeowners, manufactured housing and flood insurance, as well as voluntary manufactured housing, condominium and homeowners insurance referred to as Homeowners, and renters insurance and other products referred to as Renters and Other.

Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. and its subsidiaries provide insurance brokerage, reinsurance brokerage, consulting, and third-party property/casualty claims settlement and administration services to entities and individuals around the world. Its brokerage segment provides brokerage and consulting services to entities of all types, including commercial, nonprofit and public sector entities, insurance companies and insurance capital providers and, to a lesser extent, individuals, in the areas of insurance and reinsurance placements, risk of loss management and management of employer sponsored benefit programs, while its risk management segment provides contract claim settlement, claim administration, loss control services and risk management consulting. It believes its major strength is its ability to deliver comprehensively structured insurance, reinsurance and risk management solutions, superior claim outcomes and comprehensive consulting services to its clients.

Akamai Technologies, Inc., founded in 1998, provides solutions that help global enterprises build, secure and accelerate their applications and digital experiences, with the mission of powering and protecting life online. As of December 31, 2025, its massively distributed global infrastructure comprised more than 4,300 edge points of presence in over 130 countries and approximately 700 cities, integrated with roughly 1,200 network partners, giving it visibility into traffic volumes, congestion, attack patterns and vulnerabilities. It leverages these insights to offer security solutions that protect customers from threats and attacks, along with full-stack compute solutions for building and delivering high-performance, low-latency applications.

Albemarle Corporation, incorporated in Virginia in 1993, is a world leader in transforming essential resources into critical ingredients for mobility, energy, connectivity and health, partnering to pioneer new ways to move, power, connect and protect. The end markets it serves include grid storage, automotive, aerospace, conventional energy, electronics, construction, agriculture and food, pharmaceuticals and medical devices. The company and its joint ventures operate more than 25 production and research and development facilities plus a number of administrative facilities, and it attributes its leading position in its industries to world-class resources with reliable and consistent supply, leading process chemistry, high-impact innovation, customer centricity and a focus on people and planet.

Align Technology, Inc. is a global medical device company primarily engaged in the design, manufacture and marketing of Invisalign clear aligners for the treatment of malocclusions by orthodontists and general dental practitioners, Vivera retainers for retention, iTero intraoral scanners and services for dentistry, and exocad computer-aided design and computer-aided manufacturing software for dental laboratories and dental practitioners. Its vision and strategy is to revolutionize orthodontic and restorative dentistry through digital treatment planning and implementation using the Align Digital Platform, an integrated suite of proprietary technologies and services designed to deliver a seamless, end-to-end solution for patients, consumers, orthodontists, general dental practitioners and lab partners.

The Allstate Corporation was incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware on November 5, 1992, to serve as the holding company for Allstate Insurance Company, and is one of the largest publicly held personal lines insurers in the United States, conducting its business principally through Allstate Insurance Company and other subsidiaries. Its strategy is to increase market share in personal property-liability and broaden protection offerings, and its reportable segments are Allstate Protection, offering private passenger auto, homeowners, other personal lines and commercial insurance through exclusive agents, independent agents, contact centers and online under the Allstate, National General, Direct Auto and Answer Financial brands; Run-off Property-Liability; and Protection Services, providing consumer product protection plans, roadside assistance, automotive protection, identity protection and restoration, and mobility products.

Allegion plc is a leading global provider of security products and solutions that keep people and assets safe and secure in the places they live, learn, work and connect. It offers an extensive and versatile portfolio of security and access control products and solutions across a range of market-leading brands, including door controls, door control systems and exit devices such as panic hardware for life safety, together with electronic security, access control and identity solutions, delivered worldwide as hardware, software, services and systems by its experts and tailored to end-user security needs.

Applied Materials, Inc. is the leader in the materials engineering solutions used to produce virtually every semiconductor in the world, and is a Delaware corporation incorporated in 1967. It designs, develops, produces and services the critical wafer fabrication tools its customers need to manufacture semiconductors, whose products are used across personal computing devices, mobile phones, artificial intelligence and data center servers, automobiles, connected devices, industrial applications and consumer electronics, and it leverages the semiconductor capital equipment industry's most comprehensive portfolio of products to connect and co-optimize its technologies. It utilizes a distributed manufacturing model under which manufacturing and supply chain activities are conducted in countries including the United States, Singapore, Japan, China, Korea, Taiwan, Israel and other countries in Asia and Europe.

Amcor plc is the global leader in developing and producing responsible primary packaging solutions across a variety of materials for nutrition, health, beauty and wellness categories. Its global product innovation and sustainability expertise produces a range of flexible packaging, rigid packaging, cartons and closures that are more sustainable, functional and appealing, and in fiscal year 2026 approximately 75,000 Amcor people generated $23.5 billion in annual sales from operations spanning approximately 400 locations in more than 40 countries. It completed its merger with Berry Global Group, Inc. on April 30, 2025, and in May 2026 its Board of Directors approved a change in fiscal year end from June 30 to December 31.

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. drives innovation in high performance and AI computing, with its technology powering billions of experiences across cloud and AI infrastructure, embedded systems, AI PCs and gaming. Its broad portfolio of AI-optimized CPUs, GPUs, networking and software delivers full-stack solutions, including semi-custom system-on-chips, adaptive SoCs and accelerated processing units for clients, and for data centers AI accelerators, microprocessors, GPUs, data processing units, AI network interface cards, field programmable gate arrays, ultra-low latency networking and rack-scale data center platform designs for AI supercomputers and machine learning workloads. It was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.

AMETEK, Inc., incorporated in Delaware and whose predecessor was originally incorporated in 1930 as American Machine and Metals, Inc., is a leading global manufacturer of electronic instruments and electromechanical devices with operations in North America, Europe, Asia and South America. Its products are marketed and sold worldwide through two operating groups: Electronic Instruments, a leader in the design and manufacture of advanced instruments for the process, power and industrial, and aerospace markets; and Electromechanical, a differentiated supplier of precision motion control solutions, highly engineered medical components and devices, thermal management systems, specialty metals and electrical interconnects.

Amgen Inc. discovers, develops, manufactures and delivers innovative medicines to fight some of the world's toughest diseases, focusing on areas of high unmet medical need and leveraging its expertise to improve people's lives while reducing the social and economic burden of disease. It helped launch the biotechnology industry more than 45 years ago and has grown to be one of the world's leading independent biotechnology companies, with a robust pipeline of potential first-in-class medicines at all stages of development and a presence in approximately 100 countries. Amgen was incorporated in California in 1980, became a Delaware corporation in 1987, and operates in one operating segment, human therapeutics.

Ameriprise Financial, Inc. is a diversified financial services company with a more than 130-year history of providing solutions to help clients confidently achieve their financial objectives, operating as a holding company incorporated in Delaware that primarily engages in business through its subsidiaries. It is a long-standing leader in financial planning and advice, offering a broad range of products and services designed to assist individual and institutional clients in achieving their financial objectives, and carries out its strategy through two primary go-to-market approaches, Wealth Management and Asset Management, centered on holistic advice and on managing and protecting clients assets and income.

American Tower Corporation is one of the largest global real estate investment trusts and a leading independent owner, operator and developer of multitenant communications real estate. Its primary business, property operations, is the leasing of space on communications sites to wireless service providers, radio and television broadcast companies, wireless data providers, government agencies and municipalities, and accounted for 97 percent of total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025. It also offers tower-related services in the United States, including site application, zoning and permitting, structural and mount analyses, and construction management, and operates a data center business.

Amazon.com, Inc. seeks to be Earth's most customer-centric company and is guided by four principles: customer obsession rather than competitor focus, passion for invention, commitment to operational excellence, and long-term thinking. It has organized its operations into three segments, North America, International and Amazon Web Services, which reflect the way the company evaluates its business performance and manages its operations, and in each segment it serves primary customer sets consisting of consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, advertisers and employees.

Arista Networks, Inc. was founded to enable its customers to access all their centers of data in the quickest, most reliable and secure manner, and has emerged as an industry leader delivering data-driven, client-to-cloud networking-as-a-service. Its Centers of Data strategy is a fundamental pivot from legacy networking approaches that create incongruent silos to a unified, data-driven approach in which the network is a service that interconnects four primary domains: AI Centers, Data Centers, Campus Centers and WAN Centers. Its network-as-a-service platform is anchored by the state-oriented Extensible Operating System and Network Data Lake, and its solutions offer uncompromising reliability derived from robust quality assurance capabilities and automated diagnostics and are based on advanced open and standards-based technology. Its Arista Etherlink portfolio comprises a family of over twenty products for AI Scale Out and Scale Across use cases.

Aon plc is a leading global professional services firm that provides clients with actionable analytic insight, globally integrated Risk Capital and Human Capital expertise and locally relevant solutions, giving them the clarity and confidence to make better risk and people decisions that protect and grow their businesses. It serves clients in more than 120 countries across all market segments and nearly every industry, focuses its portfolio on higher-margin, capital-light professional services businesses with high recurring revenue streams and strong cash flow generation, and is focused on accelerating its Aon United strategy to serve clients as one globally connected firm.

A. O. Smith Corporation is a manufacturer of water heating and water treatment products operating through two reporting segments, North America and Rest of World, with the Rest of World segment primarily comprising China, India, and Europe. Both segments manufacture and market comprehensive lines of residential and commercial gas and electric water heaters, boilers, heat pumps, tanks and water treatment products. Its products include electric, natural gas and liquid propane tank-type water heaters, tankless, heat pump and solar tank units, residential and commercial boilers, water softeners and filtration systems, expansion tanks, swimming pool and spa heaters, and commercial solar water heating systems. Sales in the North America segment accounted for approximately 78 percent of total sales in 2025.

APA Corporation, whose wholly owned subsidiary is Apache Corporation, is an independent energy company that owns subsidiaries that explore for, develop and produce crude oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids. Its oil and gas operations are in three geographic areas: the U.S., Egypt, and offshore the U.K. in the North Sea, and it also has active development, exploration and appraisal operations ongoing in Suriname, as well as exploration interests in Uruguay, Alaska and other international locations.

Air Products and Chemicals, Inc., a Delaware corporation founded in 1940, is a world-leading industrial gases company that has built a reputation for innovation, operational excellence and commitment to safety and environmental stewardship, focused on serving energy, environmental and emerging markets and generating a cleaner future. It reports earnings under five segments: Americas, Asia, Europe, Middle East and India, and Corporate and other. Its regional industrial gases business produces and sells atmospheric gases such as oxygen, nitrogen and argon, process gases such as hydrogen, helium, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and syngas, and specialty gases, accounting for over 90 percent of consolidated sales in fiscal 2025, and it competes primarily with Air Liquide, Linde and Messer, distributing product through on-site and merchant supply modes under long-term contracts.

Amphenol Corporation is one of the world's largest designers, manufacturers and marketers of electrical, electronic and fiber optic connectors and interconnect systems, antennas, sensors and sensor-based products and coaxial, high-speed, fiber optic and specialty cable, serving an industry with estimated worldwide sales of approximately $500 billion in 2025. Certain predecessor businesses were founded in 1932 and the company was incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in 1986. Its strategy is to provide customers with comprehensive design capabilities, a broad selection of products and a high level of quality and service on a worldwide basis, and it aligns its businesses into three reportable business segments serving end markets that include communications networks, defense, industrial, information technology and data communications, mobile devices, automotive and commercial aerospace.

Founded in 1990, Apollo Global Management, Inc. is a high-growth global alternative asset manager and a retirement services provider that conducts its business primarily in the U.S. through three reportable segments: Asset Management, Retirement Services and Principal Investing. Its Asset Management segment focuses on credit and equity investing strategies, earning fees for providing investment management services and expertise to its client base and earning capital solutions fees alongside its private equity franchise, and it reported total assets under management of $938.4 billion as of December 31, 2025.

AppLovin Corporation provides end-to-end artificial intelligence-powered advertising solutions for businesses to reach, monetize and grow their global audience, generating revenue when advertisers achieve their return on advertising spend targets, so that their success directly fuels its growth. Its advertising solutions include Axon Ads Manager, a user acquisition solution offering advanced campaign management, real-time analytics and lifetime value reporting, and MAX, an in-app bidding solution that optimizes the value of publishers' advertising inventory by running a single unbiased, real-time competitive auction. Through its technologies and scaled distribution, advertisers can place content so it is discovered by the right audience and manage, optimize and analyze marketing investments, while publishers can better monetize their gaming apps.

Aptiv PLC is a public limited company incorporated under the laws of Jersey and resident for tax purposes in Switzerland, whose ordinary shares are publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol APTV, having been created in a December 2024 reorganization in which Old Aptiv established a new publicly listed Jersey parent company that was renamed Aptiv PLC. Aptiv supplies advanced safety, connectivity and security systems and software to the automotive sector through three reportable segments: Intelligent and Advanced Systems, providing critical technologies and services to enhance vehicle safety, security, comfort and convenience, including intelligent sensors, high-performance compute platforms and advanced software tools; Engineered Components, providing connection systems, high-performance interconnects and cable management and protection solutions; and Electrical Distribution Systems, providing low voltage and high voltage power, signal and data distribution solutions.

Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc. is a Maryland corporation formed in October 1994 that has elected to be taxed as a REIT for federal income tax purposes, and describes itself as a best-in-class, mission-driven life science REIT. It pioneered the life science real estate niche in 1994 and is the preeminent and longest-tenured owner, operator and developer of collaborative Megacampus ecosystems in AAA life science innovation cluster locations including Greater Boston, the San Francisco Bay Area, San Diego, Seattle, Maryland, Research Triangle and New York City. As of December 31, 2025 it had a total market capitalization of $20.75 billion and a North American asset base of approximately 39.4 million RSF of operating properties and new Class A/A+ development and redevelopment properties under construction, with occupancy of its operating properties of 90.9 percent.

Ares Management Corporation is a leading global alternative investment manager with $622.5 billion of assets under management and over 4,250 employees in over 55 offices in more than 25 countries. It offers its investors a range of investment strategies and seeks to deliver attractive performance to an investor base that includes over 2,850 direct institutional relationships and a significant retail investor base across its publicly-traded funds, sub-advised accounts and perpetual wealth vehicles. Since its inception in 1997 it has adhered to a disciplined investment philosophy that focuses on delivering strong risk-adjusted investment returns through market cycles, and it believes each of its distinct but complementary investment groups in Credit, Real Assets, Secondaries and Private Equity is a market leader based on assets under management and investment performance. Its assets under management grew to $622.5 billion as of December 31, 2025 from $94.0 billion a decade earlier.

Atmos Energy Corporation is a natural gas-only distributor, an S&P 500 company headquartered in Dallas and incorporated in Texas and Virginia. It safely delivers reliable, efficient and abundant natural gas through regulated sales and transportation arrangements to approximately 3.4 million residential, commercial, public authority and industrial customers in eight states located primarily in the South, and it also operates one of the largest intrastate pipelines in Texas based on miles of pipe. Its vision is to be the safest provider of natural gas services, and its operating strategy is focused on modernizing its business and infrastructure while reducing regulatory lag, supporting continued investment in safety, innovation, environmental sustainability and its communities.

Broadcom Inc. is a global technology leader that designs, develops and supplies a broad range of semiconductor and semiconductor-based solutions and infrastructure software solutions, with a more than 60-year history of innovation dating back to origins from AT&T/Bell Labs, Lucent and Hewlett-Packard that has evolved through acquisitions including LSI Corporation, Broadcom Corporation, Brocade Communications Systems, CA, Inc., Symantec Enterprise Security and VMware. It maintains design, product and software development engineering expertise and resources at locations primarily in the U.S., Asia and Europe, and combines global scale, engineering depth, broad product portfolio, superior execution and operational focus to deliver category-leading semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions. Its semiconductor solutions include high-performance Ethernet transceivers built on a proprietary digital signal processing communication architecture and fiber optic components.

Avery Dennison Corporation, founded in 1935 and incorporated in Delaware in 1977 as Avery International Corporation and renamed Avery Dennison Corporation in 1990 when it merged a subsidiary into Dennison Manufacturing Company, is a global leader in materials science and digital identification solutions. It provides branding and information solutions that optimize labor and supply chain efficiency and reduce waste, and its performance tapes products include a variety of Fasson-brand and Avery Dennison-brand tapes and other pressure-sensitive adhesive-based materials and converted products, mechanical fasteners and performance polymers, whose pressure-sensitive adhesive-based materials are used in non-mechanical fastening, bonding and sealing systems for automotive, electronics, building and construction, general industrial, personal care and medical applications.

With a history dating back to 1886, American Water Works Company is the largest and most geographically diverse publicly-traded water and wastewater utility company in the United States, as measured by both operating revenues and population served. Incorporated in Delaware in 1936 as a holding company, it employs approximately 7,000 professionals who provide drinking water, wastewater and other related services to approximately 14 million people in 24 states. It conducts the majority of its business through regulated utilities providing water and wastewater services, collectively presented as one reportable segment referred to as the Regulated Businesses, and also operates businesses that provide water and wastewater services to the U.S. government on military installations and to municipalities.

Axon Enterprise, Inc. is a technology company that provides integrated hardware and software solutions, founder-led since 1993 and grown from a mission to protect life into a global technology company serving a range of customers across the public and private sector. Its products and services allow customers to capture and use critical data to support fully-connected operational workflows, and its trusted network seamlessly integrates software and hardware with a range of connected devices, including TASER energy devices, cameras and sensors, drones and robotics, cloud-based evidence management, records management, real-time operations software, critical incident and emergency response systems, immersive training and productivity tools, all enhanced by artificial intelligence. Its subscription software as a service solutions are organized into categories including Digital Evidence Management, with Axon Evidence, a secure cloud-based platform that enables public safety to store, manage and share critical evidence while ensuring chain of custody and compliance, and Productivity Solutions, including Axon Records, Axon Standards and AI Era Plan solutions such as Real-Time Translation, Draft One, Policy Chat and Auto-Transcribe.

American Express is a global payments and premium lifestyle brand powered by technology. Founded in 1850 and headquartered in New York, its card-issuing, merchant-acquiring and card network businesses offer products and services to a broad range of customers, including consumers, small businesses, mid-sized companies and large corporations around the world. Its products and services include credit and charge cards and complementary travel, dining, lifestyle and expense management offerings, banking and other payment and financing products including deposits and non-card lending, merchant acquisition and processing, and network services, offered through channels such as mobile and online applications, affiliate marketing, third-party service providers and business partners. Worldwide processed volume was $227.2 billion for 2025 and it had 66.2 million cards-in-force issued by third parties.

AutoZone, Inc. is a leading retailer and distributor of automotive replacement parts and accessories in the Americas. It began operations in 1979 and at August 30, 2025 operated 6,627 stores in the United States, 883 stores in Mexico and 147 stores in Brazil, each carrying an extensive product line for cars, sport utility vehicles, vans and light duty trucks, including new and remanufactured automotive hard parts, maintenance items, accessories and non-automotive products. In 6,098 of its domestic stores as well as the vast majority of its stores in Mexico and Brazil it has a commercial sales program that provides prompt delivery of parts and other products and commercial credit to local, regional and national repair garages, dealers, service stations, fleet owners and other accounts, and it also sells through www.autozone.com, www.autozonepro.com and the ALLDATA brand of automotive diagnostic products.

The Boeing Company, together with its subsidiaries, is one of the world's major aerospace firms, organized based on the products and services it offers and operating in three reportable segments: Commercial Airplanes, which develops, produces and markets commercial jet aircraft principally to the commercial airline industry worldwide, offering a family of commercial jetliners that includes the 737 narrow-body model and the 767, 777 and 787 wide-body models with development continuing on the 777X program and the 737-7 and 737-10 derivatives; Defense, Space & Security, which engages in the research, development, production and modification of manned and unmanned military aircraft and weapons systems for strike, surveillance and mobility, including fighter and trainer aircraft; and Global Services.

Bank of America Corporation is a Delaware corporation, a bank holding company and a financial holding company, and one of the world's largest financial institutions, serving individual consumers, small- and middle-market businesses, institutional investors, large corporations and governments with a full range of banking, investing, asset management and other financial and risk management products and services. Its principal executive offices are located in the Bank of America Corporate Center in Charlotte, North Carolina, it employed approximately 213,000 employees at December 31, 2025 with 77 percent located in the U.S., and as part of its efforts to streamline its organizational structure and reduce complexity and costs it has reduced and intends to continue to reduce the number of its corporate subsidiaries, including through intercompany mergers.

Ball Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries are one of the world's leading suppliers of aluminum packaging for the beverage, personal care and household products industries, organized in 1880 and incorporated in Indiana in 1922. Its sustainable aluminum packaging products are produced for a variety of end uses in facilities around the world, and in 2025 its total consolidated net sales were $13.16 billion. Its largest product line is aluminum beverage containers, and it also produces extruded aluminum aerosol containers, recloseable aluminum bottles across multiple consumer categories and aluminum slugs. It sells its aluminum packaging products globally to large multinational beverage, personal care and household products companies with which it has developed long-term relationships, evidenced by its high customer retention and large number of long-term supply contracts.

Baxter International Inc., incorporated under Delaware law in 1931, provides through its subsidiaries a broad portfolio of essential healthcare products, including sterile intravenous solutions, infusion systems and devices, parenteral nutrition therapies, inhaled anesthetics, generic injectable pharmaceuticals, surgical hemostat and sealant products, advanced surgical equipment, smart bed systems, patient monitoring and diagnostic technologies, and respiratory health devices. These products are used by hospitals, nursing homes, rehabilitation centers, ambulatory surgery centers, doctors offices, kidney dialysis centers and patients at home under physician supervision. As of December 31, 2025, after giving effect to the sale of its Kidney Care business, it manufactured products in over 20 countries and sold them in over 100 countries.

Best Buy Co., Inc. was incorporated in the state of Minnesota in 1966 and is driven by its purpose to enrich lives through technology and its vision to personalize and humanize technology solutions for every stage of life, accomplishing this by leveraging its combination of tech expertise and a human touch to meet customers' everyday needs whether they come to it online, visit its stores or invite it into their homes. It has operations in the U.S. and Canada through two reportable segments, Domestic and International, with the Domestic segment comprising its operations in all states, districts and territories of the U.S. along with its Best Buy Health business, and brand names including Best Buy, Best Buy Ads, Best Buy Business, Best Buy Essentials and Geek Squad.

Becton, Dickinson and Company, incorporated under the laws of the State of New Jersey in November 1906 as successor to a New York business started in 1897 and with executive offices in Franklin Lakes, New Jersey, is a global medical technology company engaged in the development, manufacture and sale of a broad range of medical supplies, devices, laboratory equipment and diagnostic products used by healthcare institutions, physicians, life science researchers, clinical laboratories, the pharmaceutical industry and the general public. It provides customer solutions focused on improving medication management and patient safety, supporting infection prevention practices, equipping surgical and interventional procedures, improving drug delivery, aiding anesthesiology care and enhancing diagnostics, and its BD Life Sciences segment provides products for the safe collection and transport of diagnostic specimens and instruments and reagent systems to detect a broad range of infectious diseases, healthcare-associated infections and cancers.

Bloom Energy is a global leader in onsite power generation, delivering a foundational platform purpose-built for the digital era and the global energy transition. It manufactures a versatile fuel cell energy platform supporting the commercial availability of two main products, the Bloom Energy Server fuel cell system for generating electricity and the Bloom Electrolyzer for producing hydrogen, with its primary product being a proprietary high-temperature solid-oxide fuel cell technology that converts fuels including natural gas, biogas and hydrogen into electricity at high density without combustion or moving parts, achieving lower emissions and higher efficiency than legacy systems. It designs, manufactures, distributes and operates the Bloom Energy Server to provide resilient, distributed power for critical operations, serves Fortune 500 companies across the data center, semiconductor manufacturing, artificial intelligence infrastructure, utility and other industrial sectors, is headquartered in Silicon Valley, employs more than 2,000 people worldwide and manufactures its systems in the United States.

Franklin Resources, Inc. is a holding company with subsidiaries operating under its Franklin Templeton and/or subsidiary brand names, whose common stock is traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol BEN and is included in the Standard & Poor's 500 Index, and it has one operating segment, investment management and related services. It offers its services and products under various distinct brand names, including Alcentra, Apera, Benefit Street Partners, Brandywine Global Investment Management, Canvas, Clarion Partners, ClearBridge Investments, Fiduciary Trust International, Franklin Mutual Series, K2, Legg Mason, Lexington Partners and O'Shaughnessy, providing its investment management and related services to retail, institutional and high-net-worth investors in jurisdictions worldwide and delivering its investment capabilities through a variety of products and vehicles and multiple points of access, including directly to investors and through financial intermediaries.

Brown-Forman Corporation, incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in 1933 as successor to a business founded in 1870 as a partnership and later incorporated under the laws of the Commonwealth of Kentucky in 1901, primarily manufactures, distills, bottles, imports, exports, markets and sells a wide variety of beverage alcohol products under recognized brands. It employs approximately 4,900 people on six continents, including approximately 1,900 people in the United States and 700 people in Louisville, Kentucky, home of its world headquarters, and according to International Wine & Spirit Research it is the largest American-owned premium-plus spirits company. It is a controlled company under New York Stock Exchange rules because the Brown family owns more than 50 percent of its voting stock.

Bunge Global SA is a premier agribusiness solutions company, connecting farmers to consumers and delivering essential food, feed and fuel to the world, with dedicated employees, integrated operations and a global footprint that give it access to key markets and a diverse agricultural network covering major crops. With more than 200 years of experience and operations in more than 50 countries, it is a leading global oilseed processor and producer of vegetable oils and protein meal, a leading global grain merchandiser, a leading seller of packaged plant-based oils worldwide, and a leading producer and seller of wheat flours, bakery mixes and related products in South America. Its global operations include purchasing, storing, transporting, processing, selling and distributing agricultural commodities and related products.

Biogen Inc. is a global biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing and delivering innovative therapies for people living with serious and complex diseases. It has a broad portfolio of medicines to treat multiple sclerosis, has introduced the first approved treatment for spinal muscular atrophy, co-developed treatments to address a defining pathology of Alzheimer's disease and launched the first approved treatment to target a genetic cause of ALS, and it markets the first and only drug approved in the U.S., the E.U. and certain international markets for the treatment of Friedreich's ataxia in adults and adolescents aged 16 years and older. It is focused on advancing its pipeline in neurology, specialized immunology and rare diseases, supporting its efforts through internal research and development programs, external collaborations and acquisitions, with marketed products including VUMERITY, TYSABRI, TECFIDERA, AVONEX and PLEGRIDY for MS, SPINRAZA for SMA, SKYCLARYS for FA and QALSODY for ALS.

Booking Holdings Inc. aims to make it easier for everyone to experience the world, providing consumers with a best-in-class experience through tailored planning, payment, language and other options that seamlessly connect them with its travel service provider partners, offered through five primary consumer-facing brands: Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable, covering accommodations, ground transportation, flights, activities, restaurants and meta search. It derives substantially all of its revenues from providing online travel reservation services that facilitate online travel purchases by travelers from travel service providers, and also earns revenues from payment facilitation, advertising, restaurant reservation and management services, travel-related insurance offerings and other services, reporting revenues of $26.9 billion for the year ended December 31, 2025.

Baker Hughes Company is an energy technology company with a diversified portfolio of technologies and services that span the energy and industrial value chain. Built on a century of experience and conducting business in over 120 countries, its innovative technologies and services are taking energy forward, and it is well positioned to deliver solutions across industrial and energy markets that make energy safer, cleaner and more efficient, with health, safety and environment integrated into everything it does. It organizes its business into two operating segments based on the focus of its markets and on customers' buying priorities, selling through direct and indirect channels with a direct sales force that has a strong regional focus and is supported by centers of excellence in each major product line, and its Oilfield Services and Equipment segment designs and manufactures products and provides related services and integrated solutions.

BlackRock, Inc. is a leading publicly traded investment management firm with $14.0 trillion of assets under management at December 31, 2025 and approximately 24,900 employees in more than 30 countries serving clients in over 100 countries across the globe, providing a broad range of investment management and technology and subscription services to institutional and retail clients worldwide. On July 1, 2025 it completed the acquisition of 100 percent of the business and assets of HPS Investment Partners, a leading global credit investment manager, and concurrently BlackRock Finance, Inc., Global Infrastructure Management and HPS and their respective subsidiaries became wholly owned subsidiaries of BlackRock Saturn Subco, LLC. It attributes its ability to increase revenue, earnings and stockholder value over time to generating new business, including business in Aladdin and other technology products and services, and considers its ability to attract, develop and retain qualified professionals critical to that effort.

Bristol-Myers Squibb Company, incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in August 1933 under the name Bristol-Myers Company as successor to a New York business started in 1887 and renamed Bristol-Myers Squibb Company in 1989 as a result of a merger, operates in a single segment engaged in the discovery, development, licensing, manufacturing, marketing, distribution and sale of innovative medicines that help patients prevail over serious diseases. Its principal strategy is to combine the resources, scale and capability of a large pharmaceutical company with the speed, agility and focus on innovation typically found in the biotech industry, focused on discovering, developing and delivering transformational medicines for patients facing serious diseases in areas where it believes it can make a meaningful difference, including oncology, hematology, immunology, cardiovascular, neuroscience and other areas.

The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation, a Delaware corporation headquartered in New York, is a global financial services platforms company whose subsidiaries have been in business since 1784, with $59.3 trillion in assets under custody and/or administration and $2.2 trillion in assets under management as of December 31, 2025. It divides its businesses into three principal business segments: Securities Services, Market and Wealth Services, and Investment and Wealth Management, plus an Other segment that includes corporate treasury activities such as its securities portfolio, tax credit investments and other corporate investments, corporate and bank-owned life insurance, derivatives and other trading activity, and certain business exits.

description: Broadridge Financial Solutions, Inc., a Delaware corporation, is a global financial technology leader powering investing, corporate governance and communications. It delivers technology-driven solutions to banks, broker-dealers, asset and wealth managers, public companies, investors and mutual funds that enable its clients to operate, innovate and grow, helping financial services companies enhance investor engagement, optimize trading and investing and digitize communications. It operates in two reportable segments: Investor Communication Solutions, which includes Regulatory Solutions, Data-Driven Fund Solutions, Corporate Issuer Solutions and Customer Communications Solutions and represented approximately 74 percent of total revenues in fiscal years 2026 and 2025, and Global Technology and Operations, which provides automated mutual fund and exchange-traded fund trade processing, trust, trading and settlement services, and marketing and transactional communications solutions.

Berkshire Hathaway Inc. is a holding company domiciled in Delaware, with corporate headquarters in Omaha, Nebraska, owning subsidiaries engaged in numerous diverse business activities. The most important of these are insurance businesses, conducted on both a primary and a reinsurance basis, a freight rail transportation business, and a group of utility and energy generation and distribution businesses, and it also owns and operates numerous other businesses engaged in a variety of manufacturing, services and retailing activities. Its operating subsidiaries are managed on an unusually decentralized basis, with few centralized or integrated business functions, while its Chief Executive Officer is ultimately responsible for significant capital allocation decisions, investment activities and evaluating the operating performance of the operating businesses.

Brown & Brown, Inc., a Florida corporation, and its subsidiaries is a diversified insurance agency, wholesale brokerage, insurance programs and service organization that markets and sells insurance products and services, primarily in the property, casualty and employee benefits areas. It primarily operates as an agent or broker not assuming underwriting risks, while also operating and/or participating in various ancillary insurance operations, including reinsurance companies and stand-alone captives that assume underwriting risk, series captive insurance companies, protected cell companies, segregated account companies, a quota share captive and an excess of loss layer captive, which facilitate additional underwriting capacity, generate incremental revenues and/or enable it to participate in certain underwriting results. It also operates a write-your-own flood insurance carrier, Wright National.

Boston Scientific Corporation is a global developer, manufacturer and marketer of medical devices used in a broad range of interventional medical specialties, and a medical technology leader for more than 45 years that has advanced the practice of less-invasive medicine by helping physicians and other medical professionals diagnose and treat a wide range of diseases and medical conditions and improve patients' quality of life by providing alternatives to surgery and other medical procedures that are typically traumatic to the body. Its mission is to transform lives through innovative medical solutions that improve the health of patients around the world, it advances science for life by providing high-performance solutions to address unmet patient needs and reduce the cost of health care, and it operates pursuant to five strategic imperatives, with businesses including Cardiovascular and Interventional Cardiology and Vascular Therapies, which develops and manufactures technologies to diagnose and treat complex coronary, peripheral and venous diseases.

Blackstone Inc. is the world's largest alternative asset manager, seeking to deliver compelling returns for institutional and individual investors by strengthening the companies and assets in which it invests. Its more than $1.3 trillion in Total Assets Under Management as of December 31, 2025 include global investment strategies focused on real estate, private equity, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, credit, real assets, secondaries and hedge funds. It invests across asset classes on behalf of pension funds, insurance companies and individual investors using a solutions-oriented approach, and believes its scale, diversified business, long record of investment performance, rigorous investment process and strong client relationships position it to continue to perform well in a variety of market conditions, expand its assets under management and innovate.

BXP is a Delaware corporation and a fully integrated, self-administered and self-managed REIT, and one of the largest publicly-traded office REITs in the United States based on total market capitalization as of December 31, 2025, that develops, owns and manages primarily premier workplaces. BXP was formed in 1997 to succeed the real estate development, redevelopment, acquisition, management, operating and leasing businesses of its predecessor company founded by Mortimer B. Zuckerman and Edward H. Linde in 1970. Its properties are concentrated in six dynamic gateway markets, Boston, Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco, Seattle and Washington, DC, and at December 31, 2025 it owned or had joint venture interests in a portfolio of 179 commercial real estate properties aggregating approximately 52.6 million net rentable square feet of primarily premier workplaces, including eight properties under construction or redevelopment.

Citigroup is a global diversified financial services holding company whose businesses provide consumers, corporations, governments and institutions with a broad, yet focused, range of financial products and services, including consumer banking and credit, corporate and investment banking, securities brokerage, trade and securities services and wealth management. Citi does business in nearly 160 countries and jurisdictions and is managed pursuant to five reportable business segments, also referred to as Citi's five businesses.

Cardinal Health, Inc., an Ohio corporation formed in 1979, is a global healthcare services and products company providing customized solutions for hospitals, healthcare systems, pharmacies, ambulatory surgery centers, clinical laboratories, physician offices and patients in the home. It provides pharmaceuticals and medical products and cost-effective services and solutions that enhance the healthcare system and supply chain efficiency, and connects patients, providers, payers, pharmacists and manufacturers for integrated care coordination. It reports its financial results in two reportable segments, Pharmaceutical and Specialty Solutions and Global Medical Products and Distribution, with all remaining operating segments included in Other, which is comprised of Nuclear and Precision Health Solutions, at-Home Solutions and OptiFreight Logistics.

Carrier Global Corporation is a global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, focused on providing differentiated, digitally enabled lifecycle solutions to its customers. Its portfolio includes industry-leading brands such as Carrier, Viessmann, Toshiba, Automated Logic and Carrier Transicold, which offer innovative heating, cooling and cold chain solutions, and it also provides a broad array of related building services, including audit, design, installation, system integration, repair, maintenance and monitoring. Its performance-driven culture is intended to create long-term shareowner value by investing strategically to strengthen its product position in homes, buildings and across the cold chain to drive profitable growth, and it believes its business segments are well positioned to benefit from favorable secular trends, including urbanization, population growth and demographic shifts, food security and safety, and electrification.

Casey's General Stores, Inc. and its direct and indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries operate convenience stores primarily under the names Casey's and Caseys General Store throughout 19 states, approximately half of which are located in Iowa, Missouri and Illinois. As of April 30, 2026 there were 2,944 stores in operation, with approximately 71 percent of all stores opened in areas with populations of fewer than 20,000 persons, and it competes on the basis of traditional features of convenience store operations such as location, extended hours, product offerings, price and quality of service. All stores carry a broad selection of food items, including prepared foods such as regular and breakfast pizza, donuts, hot breakfast items and hot and cold sandwiches, beverages, tobacco and nicotine products, groceries, health and beauty aids and automotive products. Its flagship prepared food product is pizza, which it began selling in 1984 and which is available in almost all stores, served as grab-and-go slices and made-to-order whole pies, alongside hot and made-to-order sandwiches, salads, wraps, fries and bakery items including donuts and cookies.

Originally organized as Caterpillar Tractor Co. in 1925 in California and reorganized as Caterpillar Inc. in 1986 in Delaware, Caterpillar Inc., with 2025 sales and revenues of $67.589 billion, is shaping the future as the world's leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, off-highway diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives. Backed by one of the largest independent global dealer networks and financing services through Cat Financial, its primary business segments of Power & Energy, Construction Industries and Resource Industries solve customers' toughest challenges through commercial excellence and advanced technology, driven by a highly skilled, dedicated global team, and in 2025 the company introduced a revised strategy anchored by a new mission statement.

Chubb Limited is the Swiss-incorporated holding company of the Chubb Group of Companies, headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, and together with its direct and indirect subsidiaries forms a global insurance and reinsurance organization serving the needs of a diverse group of clients worldwide, with total assets of $272 billion and total shareholders' equity of $74 billion excluding noncontrolling interests at December 31, 2025. Incorporated in 1985, when it opened its first business office in Bermuda, it has grown through increased premium volume, expansion of product offerings and geographic reach and the acquisition of other companies to become a global property and casualty leader, and it expanded its personal accident and supplemental health and life insurance business with the acquisition of Cigna's business in several Asian markets in 2022. Its Commercial Insurance operations provide a broad range of property and casualty, financial lines, and accident and health products targeted to U.S. and Canadian-based middle market and small commercial customers in a variety of industries.

Cboe Global Markets, Inc., which describes itself as the world's leading derivatives and securities exchange network, delivers trading, clearing and investment solutions to people around the world, providing trading solutions and products in multiple asset classes including equities, derivatives and foreign exchange across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. Its subsidiaries include the largest options exchange and the third largest equities exchange operator in the United States, and it is committed to building a trusted, inclusive global marketplace that enables people to pursue a sustainable financial future. It reports five segments, and its Cboe Data Vantage business includes access and capacity fees to its markets, proprietary market data fees from various licensing agreements and proprietary indices, and other data and access products and services.

CBRE Group, Inc. is the world's largest commercial real estate services and investments firm based on 2025 revenue, deriving competitive advantage from its considerable scale and ability to offer integrated solutions for real estate investors and occupiers in more than 100 countries. It is a global market leader in most of its business lines and drives significant growth by helping clients optimize real estate costs, value, investment returns and workplace experiences, with those capabilities combined with an extensive knowledge platform of research, data and strategy that generated superior outcomes for clients including nearly 90 percent of Fortune 100 companies and many of the world's largest institutional real estate investors in 2025. Its strategy achieves growth across four dimensions of its business, geographies, clients, property types and services, and its Project Management segment delivers program management, project management and cost consultancy services globally through Turner & Townsend, in which it now owns 70 percent of the combined entity.

Crown Castle International Corp. owns, operates and leases shared communications infrastructure that is geographically dispersed throughout the U.S., including more than 40,000 towers and other structures such as rooftops, approximately 105,000 small cell nodes either currently generating revenue or under contract, and approximately 90,000 route miles of fiber primarily supporting small cells and fiber solutions, which it refers to collectively as communications infrastructure. Its operating segments historically consisted of Towers and Fiber, and on March 13, 2025 management signed a definitive agreement to sell its Fiber segment, with Zayo Group Holdings Inc. acquiring the fiber solutions business and an EQT Active Core Infrastructure fund acquiring the small cells business. Its strategy to create long-term stockholder value is based on its belief that there will be considerable future demand for its towers based on the location of its assets and the rapid and continuing growth in the demand for data.

Carnival Corporation was incorporated in Panama in 1974 and Carnival plc was incorporated in England and Wales in 2000, and together they operate a dual listed company whose businesses are combined through a number of contracts and provisions in their governing documents, so that the two companies operate as if they are a single economic enterprise with a single executive management team and identical Boards of Directors, while each retains its separate legal identity, stock exchange listing and shareholders. Carnival Corporation & plc is the largest global cruise company, and among the largest leisure travel companies, with a portfolio of world-class cruise lines: AIDA Cruises, Carnival Cruise Line, Costa Cruises, Cunard, Holland America Line, P&O Cruises, Princess Cruises and Seabourn.

Cadence Design Systems, Inc. is a global technology leader that develops computational, AI-driven software, accelerated hardware and silicon intellectual property products and solutions. Its customers include semiconductor companies that design and manufacture integrated circuits, as well as systems companies that design and manufacture electromechanical systems containing various types of semiconductor and other electronics, and its products and solutions empower customers to design, verify and bring to life new and innovative products. Its mission is to empower the world's most innovative companies to deliver extraordinary electronic products that drive the global economy and improve everyday life, and aligned with its Intelligent System Design strategy it organizes its offerings into three tightly integrated product categories: Core EDA, Semiconductor IP, and System Design and Analysis.

CDW Corporation, a Fortune 500 company and member of the S&P 500 Index, is a leading multi-brand provider of information technology solutions to business, government, education and healthcare customers in the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada. Its broad array of offerings ranges from discrete hardware and software products to integrated IT solutions and services including on-premise and cloud capabilities across hybrid infrastructure, digital experience and security. It is vendor, technology and consumption model unbiased, offering a broad selection of products and multi-branded IT solutions delivered in physical, virtual and cloud-based environments through approximately 10,500 customer-facing coworkers, and it is a leading sales channel partner for many original equipment manufacturers, software publishers and cloud providers. Its U.S. business, approximately 90 percent of net sales, has five dedicated customer channels, corporate, small business, government, education and healthcare, each of which generated $1.7 billion or greater in net sales in 2025, while net sales to customers in the UK and Canada combined generated $2.7 billion.

Constellation Energy Corporation is a Pennsylvania corporation that became an independent, publicly traded company in February 2022 when Exelon completed the separation of its competitive generation and customer-facing energy businesses, conducted through Constellation and its subsidiaries, by distributing all outstanding shares of the company's common stock on a pro rata basis to the holders of Exelon's common stock, with the company holding all the interests in Constellation previously held by Exelon. It describes itself as the nation's largest producer of clean and reliable energy and, following the Calpine merger, the largest private-sector power producer in the world, and it has five reportable segments representing the different geographic regions in which its owned generating resources are located and its customer-facing activities are conducted, including Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, New York and ERCOT.

CF Industries Holdings, Inc. states that its mission is to provide clean energy to feed and fuel the world sustainably, and with its employees focused on safe and reliable operations, environmental stewardship and disciplined capital and corporate management it is on a path to decarbonize its ammonia production network, the world's largest, to enable low-carbon hydrogen and nitrogen products for energy, fertilizer, emissions abatement and other industrial activities. At its core, CF Industries, a 100 percent owned subsidiary, is a producer of ammonia, using the Haber-Bosch process to fix atmospheric nitrogen with hydrogen from natural gas to produce anhydrous ammonia, which it sells as ammonia itself or upgrades to products such as granular urea, UAN and DEF, with a majority of its ammonia and ammonia-derived products used as fertilizer, as the nitrogen content provides energy essential for crop growth.

Citizens Financial Group, Inc. is headquartered in Providence, Rhode Island, and offers a broad range of retail and commercial banking products and services to individuals, small businesses, middle-market companies, large corporations and institutions, offered through more than 1,000 branches in 14 states and the District of Columbia and 75 retail and commercial non-branch offices, though certain lines of business serve national markets. At December 31, 2025 it had total assets of $226.4 billion, total deposits of $183.3 billion and total stockholders' equity of $26.3 billion, plus total client assets of $61.9 billion including assets under management of $35.9 billion and transactional assets of $26.0 billion. It is a bank holding company incorporated under Delaware state law in 1984 whose primary federal regulator is the Federal Reserve Board.

Church & Dwight Co., Inc. was founded in 1846 and incorporated in Delaware in 1925, and it develops, manufactures and markets a broad range of consumer household and personal care products and specialty products focused on animal and food production, chemicals and cleaners. Its well-recognized brands include ARM & HAMMER baking soda, cat litter, laundry detergent, carpet deodorizer and other baking soda-based products; OXICLEAN stain removers, cleaning solutions, laundry detergents and bleach alternatives; BATISTE dry shampoo; WATERPIK water flossers; THERABREATH oral care products; HERO acne treatment products; TOUCHLAND hand sanitizers; TROJAN condoms, lubricants and vibrators; FIRST RESPONSE home pregnancy and ovulation test kits; NAIR depilatories; ORAJEL oral analgesic; XTRA laundry detergent; and ZICAM cold shortening and relief products, and seven of those brands are designated as power brands because they compete in large categories and it believes they have the potential for significant global expansion, with net sales to its largest customer, Walmart Inc. and its affiliates, approximately 23 percent of consolidated net sales in each of 2025, 2024 and 2023.

C.H. Robinson Worldwide, Inc. is one of the largest global logistics providers in the world, with consolidated total revenues of $16.2 billion in 2025, and describes itself as a leader in Lean artificial intelligence supply chains. It delivers tailored logistics solutions worldwide via truckload, less-than-truckload, ocean, air and more, combining human insight with Lean AI so supply chains move faster, smarter and more sustainably, and it operates throughout North America, Europe, Asia, Oceania, South America and the Middle East. Its global suite of multimodal logistics services brings together the expertise of its people with custom technology differentiated by one of the largest datasets on shipments, routings and carriers in the world, and in November 2024 it launched C.H. Robinson Managed Solutions to give shippers seamless access to 4PL services, 3PL managed transportation and transportation management system technology from one provider.

Charter Communications, Inc. is a leading broadband connectivity company with services available to 58 million homes and small to large businesses across 41 states through its Spectrum brand. Founded in 1993, it has evolved from providing cable TV to streaming, and from high-speed Internet to a converged broadband, WiFi and mobile experience, and over the Spectrum Fiber Broadband Network and supported by its 100 percent U.S.-based employees it offers seamless connectivity and entertainment with Spectrum Internet, Mobile, TV and Voice products. Its strategy is focused on utilizing its fiber-powered network to deliver high-quality, competitively priced products with outstanding service, allowing it to increase both the number of customers it serves over its network and the number of products it sells to each customer, which reduces service transactions per relationship, yields higher customer satisfaction and lower customer churn, lowers costs to acquire and serve customers and drives greater profitability.

The Cigna Group, together with its subsidiaries, is a global health company committed to creating a better future for every individual and every community, powered by its dedicated people and valued brands, advancing its mission to improve the health and vitality of those it serves by staying grounded in the needs of its customers and patients and delivering a personalized, transparent and affordable health care experience, and focusing on leading the way to partner and innovate solutions for better health. Its global workforce of approximately 67,700 colleagues strives to fulfill that mission for more than 185 million customer relationships in more than 30 markets and jurisdictions as of December 31, 2025.

Ciena is a network technology company, providing hardware, software, and services to a wide range of network operators and enabling enhanced network capacity, service delivery, and automation, with solutions that support network traffic across a wide range of applications, including cloud, voice, video, data and artificial intelligence, and which are used globally by cloud providers, service providers and other network operators across multiple industry verticals.
